prompt: Vitrine layout: main content with a sidebar, for the few pages that need one (e.g. a form with suggestions beside it).
shortDesc: Two columns: main content plus a sidebar (right by default), stacking on phones with the sidebar after. Put slot="main" on each main-column child and slot="aside" on each sidebar child: a g-page-section in either slot drops its band padding and background and just gives its children a heading, so g-split supplies the page padding (28px 16px, 48px 32px from 860px, the section rhythm) and can follow g-site-header directly. Don't put g-split inside a g-page-section or another padded wrapper, and don't leave a g-page-section in it without a slot attribute (it would keep its band padding and be indented twice). Optional and rarely needed: artwork, artist, collection, search and exhibition pages lay themselves out; it suits a form page with suggestions beside it. Complete /exhibitions/new example (the level="1" section is the page h1 and holds the form, as g-exhibition-form requires): <g-split aside-width="wide"><g-page-section slot="main" level="1" kicker="Your exhibitions" heading="Start an exhibition"><g-exhibition-form></g-exhibition-form></g-page-section><g-page-section slot="aside" heading="Works to build around"><g-artwork-grid limit="4" min-width="150"></g-artwork-grid></g-page-section></g-split>. Attributes: aside-width="narrow" (300px, default) or "wide" (380px); aside-side="left" or "right" (default); sticky (no value) keeps the sidebar in view. With an empty aside the main column takes the full width.

props.name: aside-side
props.description: left or right (default). On phones the sidebar always comes after the main content.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Boolean attribute (write sticky with no value) to keep the sidebar in view while the main column scrolls; a sidebar taller than the window scrolls on its own and becomes keyboard-focusable. Omit it to turn it off (sticky="false" is also treated as off, but don't write it).

slots.name: main
slots.description: Main column, stacked with 24px gaps (put slot="main" on each child). A g-page-section here drops its band padding; use level="1" when it holds the page title.
Also the main column, for children without a slot attribute (after the slot="main" ones). Don't put g-page-section here: without a slot attribute it keeps its full band padding.

slots.name: aside
slots.description: Sidebar content, stacked with 24px gaps (put slot="aside" on each child). A g-page-section here drops its band padding and background; use level="3" when the main column has h2 headings.

styling.tailwindClasses: grid grid-cols-1 min-[860px]:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_300px] gap-8 min-[860px]:gap-10 max-w-[1240px] mx-auto px-4 py-7 min-[860px]:px-8 min-[860px]:py-12
styling.notes: Vitrine: a quiet gallery wall. Layout only, no colours of its own (children bring the wall/paper tones). Grid of minmax(0,1fr) plus 300px or 380px, 40px gap (32px stacked), 1240px max, centred, padding 28px 16px (48px 32px from 860px, the same rhythm as a g-page-section band, so it never sits flush on the header or footer). One column below 860px with main first. With sticky (any value but "false") the aside is position:sticky; top:24px; align-self:start with a 4px inset so focus rings aren't clipped, and gets tabindex=0 while it overflows. Driven by :host attribute selectors, so attribute changes restyle instantly. Columns are a div and an <aside> (the page already owns <main id="main">).
